title: Hormone Test Kit Repeat-Test Adherence Fact Table
scenario: An at-home diagnostics platform ships hormone test kits on a subscription. Users receive kits monthly or quarterly. The care team needs to track adherence to repeat-test cadence.
prompt:
STAKEHOLDER CONTEXT

You met with the care coordination team. The fact table you're designing will populate a daily dashboard. The dashboard needs:

- Test completion rate: count of kits with results_submitted event divided by count of kits shipped, by subscription_tier
- Adherence to cadence: count of patients who submitted results within the expected window divided by count of patients due for a test, by cohort
- Median time-to-completion: median days between kit_shipped and results_submitted, by kit_type
- Dropout rate: count of patients who did not submit results for 2 consecutive cycles divided by count of active subscribers, by cohort

VOLUME AND UPDATE FREQUENCY

- Daily source volume: ~5,000 kit lifecycle events per day
- Dashboard freshness need: daily (refreshed at 6am)
- Total fact rows after 1 year: ~300,000 rows (one row per kit_id)

WHAT YOU HAVE IN SOURCE

- Source event table: kit_lifecycle_events at event grain (one row per state change)
- dim_patient: patient_id, cohort, enrollment_date, subscription_tier, expected_cadence_days
- dim_kit_type: kit_type_id, kit_name, test_panel, turnaround_days_sla
- dim_date: date_key, calendar attributes
- dim_subscription: subscription_id, tier, interval, start_date, end_date

event_type values: kit_shipped, results_submitted, kit_returned_unused, subscription_paused, subscription_canceled. Each kit_id appears once for kit_shipped and zero-or-one times for results_submitted or kit_returned_unused. Subscription events do not have kit_id.

YOUR TASK

Design the FACT TABLE that the dashboard reads from. Dims are already built — you specify how to JOIN them and what SCD type each is. Use the response form in section 2 to record your design choices.
instructions: Fill out each form field in section 2 (the schema design response form). Dropdowns are used where the answer set is finite (SCD types, idempotency strategies, late-arriving handling); text fields for grain, fact columns, and rationale. Click Get Schema Design Feedback to grade. Reference answer runs 200-400 words across 4-6 headed sections — this is a structured design deliverable, not a terse PAA-style answer.
expected_themes: dbt tests: unique kit_id, not_null shipped_ts
reference_answer:
## Business Process
A patient receives a hormone test kit, submits a sample, and results are released. One kit lifecycle = one fact row.

## Grain
One row per kit_id (~300K rows after 1 year). Each kit appears once. Grain matches the dashboard's unit of analysis: kit completion rate and time-to-completion are kit-level metrics.

## Fact Columns
kit_id (PK), patient_id (FK), kit_type_id (FK), subscription_id (FK), shipped_ts, results_submitted_ts, returned_unused_ts, is_completed (derived: results_submitted_ts IS NOT NULL), is_adherent (derived: results_submitted_ts <= shipped_ts + expected_cadence_days), days_to_completion (derived: results_submitted_ts - shipped_ts).

## Dim Joins
dim_patient (patient_id) — Type 2 for subscription_tier changes, cohort is immutable. dim_kit_type (kit_type_id) — Type 1, kit panel definitions are static. dim_subscription (subscription_id) — Type 2 for tier changes, interval changes. dim_date (shipped_date_key) — Type 0.

## dbt Models
stg_kit_lifecycle_events: clean event_type, deduplicate duplicates, cast timestamps. int_kit_facts: pivot event grain to kit grain (one row per kit_id), FIRST_VALUE(event_ts) FILTER WHERE event_type = 'results_submitted'. mart_kit_adherence: join dims, add derived columns (is_adherent, days_to_completion). Incremental on kit_id, idempotent to late-arriving results_submitted events (upsert on kit_id).

## Tests
unique kit_id, not_null shipped_ts, relationships kit_id -> dim_patient.patient_id, accepted_values event_type IN (kit_shipped, results_submitted, kit_returned_unused).

## Edge Cases
Late-arriving results_submitted events: upsert on kit_id overwrites NULL results_submitted_ts. Kits returned unused: is_completed = FALSE, days_to_completion = NULL. Subscription tier change mid-cycle: subscription_id FK points to the tier active at shipped_ts (SCD Type 2 lookup).

grading_rubric.description: States one row per kit_id with row count estimate; ties grain to the metric asks (kit completion rate and time-to-completion are kit-level); explains why event grain or patient grain would not work.

Includes shipped_ts, results_submitted_ts (nullable), is_completed (derived Boolean), days_to_completion (derived INT); excludes attributes that belong in dims (cohort, kit_name, tier); includes surrogate FK subscription_id for Type 2 subscription dim.

dim_subscription Type 2 (tier/interval changes mid-subscription); dim_patient Type 2 (tier changes) or Type 1 (cohort immutable); dim_kit_type Type 1 (static panel definitions); rationale references whether history is needed for the metric.
Names upsert on kit_id for late results_submitted events; incremental materialization with unique_key = kit_id; explains that results_submitted_ts NULL is overwritten when the event arrives late.
At least 2 tests with column names: unique kit_id, not_null shipped_ts, relationships patient_id -> dim_patient.patient_id, or accepted_values for derived is_completed.

hints: The dashboard asks include 'count of kits with results_submitted' — that tells you the fact grain is kit-level, not event-level.
Adherence to cadence requires comparing results_submitted_ts to shipped_ts + expected_cadence_days. The expected_cadence_days comes from dim_patient or dim_subscription.
Subscription tier can change mid-cycle. If you store tier as a fact column, you lose history. If you FK to dim_subscription with SCD Type 2, you preserve the tier active at shipped_ts.
common_mistakes: Storing at event grain (one row per kit_shipped, one row per results_submitted) instead of one row per kit_id — breaks unique kit count logic.
Treating dim_subscription as Type 1 — loses the ability to report which tier the patient was on when the kit shipped.
Omitting is_completed and is_adherent as derived columns — forces BI queries to recompute the logic every time.
Not handling late-arriving results_submitted events — leads to kits永久ly marked as incomplete when the event arrives after the daily batch.
Putting the adherence business rule (results_submitted_ts <= shipped_ts + expected_cadence_days) in stg_ instead of int_ or mart_.
schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE kit_lifecycle_events (
  event_id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  kit_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  patient_id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  subscription_id BIGINT,
  kit_type_id INT NOT NULL,
  event_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  event_ts TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);

candidate_dimensions.name: dim_subscription
candidate_dimensions.description: tier, interval (monthly/quarterly), start_date, end_date, SCD Type 2

worked_example_per_field.business_process:
Answer: A patient receives a hormone test kit, submits a sample, and results are released. One kit lifecycle = one fact row.

Why: The prompt's event_type values (kit_shipped, results_submitted, kit_returned_unused) map to the lifecycle stages of a single kit. Each kit_id appears once for kit_shipped and zero-or-one times for results_submitted. The dashboard metrics (completion rate, time-to-completion) are kit-level aggregations, so the fact table grain is one row per kit_id.
worked_example_per_field.grain:
Answer: One row per kit_id (~300,000 rows after 1 year).

Why: The prompt explicitly states '~300,000 rows (one row per kit_id)' under VOLUME. The dashboard asks for 'count of kits with results_submitted' and 'median days between kit_shipped and results_submitted' — both are kit-level metrics. Event grain (multiple rows per kit_id) would break unique kit counts. Patient grain would lose the kit-level time-to-completion.
worked_example_per_field.fact_columns:
Answer: kit_id (PK), patient_id (FK), kit_type_id (FK), subscription_id (FK), shipped_ts, results_submitted_ts (nullable), returned_unused_ts (nullable), is_completed (derived Boolean), is_adherent (derived Boolean), days_to_completion (derived INT).

Why: The dashboard asks for 'count of kits with results_submitted' (requires results_submitted_ts), 'median days between kit_shipped and results_submitted' (requires shipped_ts and results_submitted_ts), and 'adherence to cadence' (requires is_adherent derived from results_submitted_ts <= shipped_ts + expected_cadence_days). Storing raw timestamps plus derived flags lets BI queries slice by any dim without recomputing the logic.
worked_example_per_field.key_strategy:
Answer: kit_id is natural PK. subscription_id is surrogate FK to dim_subscription (SCD Type 2).

Why: The prompt says 'each kit_id appears once for kit_shipped' — kit_id is already a unique natural key. subscription_id is a surrogate FK because dim_subscription is Type 2 (tier and interval can change mid-subscription). The FK points to the subscription_sk row valid at the time of kit_shipped, capturing which tier the patient was on when the kit shipped.
worked_example_per_field.dim_joins:
Answer: dim_patient (patient_id), dim_kit_type (kit_type_id), dim_subscription (subscription_id), dim_date (shipped_date_key and results_submitted_date_key).

Why: The dashboard asks include 'by subscription_tier' (requires dim_subscription), 'by cohort' (requires dim_patient), and 'by kit_type' (requires dim_kit_type). dim_date adds calendar context for weekly/monthly rollups and fiscal-year reporting.
worked_example_per_field.scd_per_dim:
Answer: dim_subscription Type 2 (tier/interval changes). dim_patient Type 2 (tier changes) or Type 1 (cohort immutable). dim_kit_type Type 1 (static panel definitions).

Why: subscription_tier can change mid-cycle (patient upgrades from monthly to quarterly) — Type 2 preserves the tier active at kit_shipped time, needed for accurate 'completion rate by subscription_tier' reporting. dim_patient.cohort is assigned at enrollment and never changes (Type 1), but if subscription_tier is stored in dim_patient, it must be Type 2. dim_kit_type panel definitions are static (Type 1).
worked_example_per_field.conformed_dims:
Answer: dim_patient is conformed across fact_kit_adherence and fact_telehealth_visits (if the platform has multiple product lines). dim_date is conformed across all facts.

Why: If the platform offers both test kits and telehealth visits, dim_patient must have the same grain and attributes (patient_id, cohort, enrollment_date) in both facts. Conformed dims let you build cross-product cohort analyses (patients who ordered a kit AND booked a visit) without rebuilding the dim.
worked_example_per_field.models:
Answer: stg_kit_lifecycle_events: clean event_type, deduplicate duplicates, cast timestamps. int_kit_facts: pivot event grain to kit grain (one row per kit_id), FIRST_VALUE(event_ts) FILTER WHERE event_type='results_submitted'. mart_kit_adherence: join dims, add derived columns (is_adherent, days_to_completion). Materialized as incremental table.

Why: stg_ cleans raw data (no business rules). int_ does the heavy reusable join work (pivot event grain to kit grain). mart_ applies business logic (is_adherent = results_submitted_ts <= shipped_ts + expected_cadence_days). Incremental materialization on kit_id keeps the daily batch fast (only new kits + updated kits).
worked_example_per_field.tests:
Answer: unique kit_id, not_null shipped_ts, relationships patient_id -> dim_patient.patient_id, accepted_values event_type IN ('kit_shipped','results_submitted','kit_returned_unused').

Why: unique kit_id ensures the grain is enforced. not_null shipped_ts ensures every fact row has a start timestamp. relationships test ensures no orphaned patient_id FKs. accepted_values on event_type catches bad source data before it pollutes the fact table.
worked_example_per_field.idempotency:
Answer: Upsert on kit_id. Late-arriving results_submitted events overwrite NULL results_submitted_ts. Incremental materialization with unique_key = kit_id.

Why: The prompt says 'results_submitted events can arrive late'. If you INSERT on every batch, you get duplicate kit_id rows. Upsert on kit_id ensures one row per kit_id: when a late results_submitted event arrives, the existing row is updated (results_submitted_ts changes from NULL to the event_ts). This keeps the fact table idempotent to replay and late arrivals.
worked_example_per_field.late_arriving:
Answer: Results_submitted events can arrive days after kit_shipped. Upsert on kit_id ensures the fact row is updated when the event finally arrives. No need to re-state closed periods — just update the single kit row.

Why: The prompt explicitly warns 'late-arriving results_submitted events'. Without upsert, a kit shipped on Monday and marked incomplete on Tuesday would stay incomplete forever if the results_submitted event arrives Wednesday. Upsert on kit_id lets the incremental model update results_submitted_ts and is_completed when the late event arrives, without rebuilding the entire fact table.
worked_example_per_field.edge_cases:
Answer: (1) Kits returned unused: is_completed = FALSE, days_to_completion = NULL. (2) Subscription tier change mid-cycle: subscription_id FK points to the tier active at shipped_ts (SCD Type 2 lookup). (3) Late-arriving results_submitted events: upsert on kit_id overwrites NULL results_submitted_ts.

Why: The prompt lists event_type = 'kit_returned_unused' — these kits never have results_submitted, so is_completed must be FALSE. If a patient upgrades from monthly to quarterly mid-cycle, the fact row must FK to the subscription_sk active at kit_shipped time, not the current subscription_sk. Late-arriving events are handled by the upsert logic described above.
